title: Inject crash hook via NODE_OPTIONS on Windows, not PATH wrapper
context: On Windows, shell-less spawnSync resolves only .exe/.com files; .cmd wrappers are invisible to libuv. The POSIX PATH-wrapper strategy for intercepting git calls during crash injection cannot work.
decision: Create git.exe as a node.exe copy. Load a hijack module via NODE_OPTIONS --import that patches child_process.spawn/spawnSync/execFileSync to intercept git calls. Guard the hijack with argv0 detection so it only runs when git.exe is the entry point, not in other node processes.
consequences: Crash hook injection moves from process spawn layer (PATH resolution) to runtime layer (import hooking)
Crash hook now works on Windows despite libuv's executable-type filtering
Requires NODE_OPTIONS coordination between CLI launcher and git.exe shim
Argv0-guarded, so no-op in CLI's own node processes—simpler than checking all call sites
alternatives_rejected: cmd.exe wrapper (dies parsing git's own flags before --import runs)
Rename git.exe as entry point without import hijack (args not rewritten in time)
